prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: high-fidelity desktop financial operations web app UI comp
Primary request: Create one production-ready 1500×1050 desktop UI comp for “Alloc” in the approved “Quiet Operator” redesign. Linear-inspired in rigor and density, but original and not a copy. This is an authenticated operational product screen, not a marketing page.

Scene/backdrop: Full-bleed desktop application screenshot. Warm crisp gray main canvas (#F4F3F0 range) with a narrow muted charcoal sidebar (#292B2E range). Flat color fields only.

Style/medium: Pixel-sharp high-fidelity SaaS interface design. Humanist sans throughout, including all money figures; tabular numerals. Compact, predictable 44px–52px header bars, restrained 1px hairline borders, tight spacing, excellent hierarchy, dense but calm. Minimal corner radius, approximately 4–6px. The broad work surface dominates.

Composition/framing: Exactly 1500×1050 landscape. Left sidebar about 190px wide. Brand “Alloc” at top, then icon+label navigation: Overview active, Requests, Memory, Forecast, Activity. Small company section and quiet signed-in user footer. Main top bar includes Northstar Fieldworks selector on the left and small controls/status on the right. Below it, a compact page header: “Overview”, a one-line timestamp/context, a visible neutral badge reading “SYNTHETIC MOCK DATA”, and a small green “Contract valid” status.

Main content uses a two-column composition: left work surface roughly 68%, right review inspector roughly 32%, separated by a clear vertical gutter and hairline structure. Do not make a decorative card grid.

Left work surface: one wide continuous section titled “Budget & exposure” with a period control “Q3 · Quarter to date”. At top, a single aligned four-column summary strip inside the same surface, not separate cards. Show these exact values verbatim:
“Authorized” “$500”
“Recognized” “$120”
“Committed” “$210”
“Available” “$170”
Add small supporting labels: “Binding hard cap”, “Posted”, “Approved, not spent”, “Remaining headroom”. Beneath, show a clean horizontal stacked exposure bar consistent with 24% recognized, 42% committed, 34% available, using neutral gray plus restrained emerald semantic fill. Include a compact ledger-style table titled “Field engineering” with columns Category, Recognized, Committed, Status. Directly beside the title show the exact phrase “scope view — not additive”. Rows may include Travel, Software, Equipment. Keep all table numbers aligned and plausible, while the four exact canonical totals above remain visually dominant. Below, continue within the broad work surface with a compact “Recent activity” table of 4–5 rows, quiet status labels, timestamps, and source/provenance snippets.

Right side: one persistent flat inspector panel titled “Review” with an amber semantic “PENDING” badge. It must show:
“Cumulative amendment limit exceeded”
“The request remains at its last approved exposure until a human decides.”
“Buffalo pilot trip”
“Revised total” “$240”
“Cumulative change” “+$60”
“Requester” “Maya Chen”
“Policy signal” “Amendment threshold exceeded”
Include a compact comparison row such as “Prior approved $180 → Revised $240”. End with one clear emerald primary button “Review request” and quiet authority copy: “Authenticated human decision · mocked for demonstration”. The inspector should feel focused and actionable, not like paper or a floating decorative card.

Color palette: Warm gray and charcoal neutrals dominate. Use emerald only for verified/available/action states, amber only for pending/review, red only for exception emphasis, and blue only for links or provenance. No accent colors used decoratively.

Text (verbatim): “Alloc”; “Overview”; “Requests”; “Memory”; “Forecast”; “Activity”; “Northstar Fieldworks”; “SYNTHETIC MOCK DATA”; “Contract valid”; “Budget & exposure”; “Authorized”; “$500”; “Recognized”; “$120”; “Committed”; “$210”; “Available”; “$170”; “Field engineering”; “scope view — not additive”; “Review”; “PENDING”; “Cumulative amendment limit exceeded”; “Buffalo pilot trip”; “Revised total”; “$240”; “Cumulative change”; “+$60”; “Maya Chen”; “Review request”.

Constraints: Exact money totals and review amounts must be legible and correct. Preserve the semantic distinction between canonical company totals and the scoped department view. Use humanist sans typography only. Use tabular numerals. Crisp straight-on screenshot, no device frame, no browser chrome, no people, no illustration, no watermark.

Avoid: field-ledger paper; ruled paper; punched holes; binder holes; handwriting; margin notes; serif finance display; any serif type; paper texture; material metaphors; gradients; glassmorphism; transparency effects; shadows suggesting floating paper; decorative card grid; giant hero metric; oversized empty space; pill-heavy UI; rounded fintech tiles; colorful charts; copied Linear branding or exact layout.
